item.title: Binance crypto exchange's $6.3 bn heist rattles crypto, draws scrutiny
item.description: The US agencies are coordinating with private-sector partners to assess the breach and recover stolen funds, while Binance pledged to cover all losses ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Myles Miller, Emily Nicolle and Scott Patterson US law enforcement joined the hunt for hackers who drained more than $6 billion from the Binance crypto exchange in the biggest cyber theft ever recorded. The Federal Bureau of Investigation is aware of the incident and is coordinating with its partners “to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate potential impacts, and coordinate appropriate investigative steps,” the agency said in a statement to Bloomberg News on Friday. Secret Service investigators are also “working around the clock” with the private sector to recover stolen funds, a spokesperson said. The Justice Department is aware of reports about the attack but does not comment on investigations, a spokesperson said.  While the full details of the Binance breach have yet to emerge, the incident comes amid growing concern about the risks posed by hackers in the age of artificial intelligence. Other recent cyberattacks have hit prediction market Polymarket, South Korean financial firms Mirae Asset Global Investments Co. and Daishin Securities, as well as Japanese currency trading platform GMO Internet Group Inc. The world’s largest crypto trading platform suspended withdrawals and pledged to cover all losses. The exchange is able to do so as a result of its ongoing investment of revenue into cryptocurrencies, Binance co-Chief Executive Officer Richard Teng said in a video posted on social media on Friday. Yi He, who is co-CEO, said Binance’s revenue for this year would completely cover the amount lost. Withdrawals were expected to resume by Sunday. “Most of what we earn from day-to-day operations is held in cryptoassets,” Teng said. “That is precisely why we are able to absorb a loss of this size, immediately, with our own money.”   Americans are prohibited from using the exchange. Binance.US is a smaller, separate entity.  The hack comes at a time when the Trump administration and its regulators have been pushing for mainstream adoption of cryptocurrencies and blockchain technology. In September, the Securities and Exchange Commission approved the so-called Innovation Exemption, which allows for public company stocks to trade on blockchains. The Binance hack is likely to raise concerns among public company executives about adopting such technology, experts said. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission, for its part, recently unveiled a proposal to regulate digital asset transactions and markets. If finalized, the measure would regulate leveraged crypto trades offered to retail customers and establish a new category for crypto exchanges offering the leveraged trades to register with the agency. “There need to be delays and checkpoints” in transactions, said Austin Campbell, a crypto expert and former banker who is now an adjunct professor at the NYU Stern School of Business, drawing an analogy to automobile safety. “The car can be faster, cheaper and more gas efficient if we take out all the airbags and seatbelts,” he said.       Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs, Chainalysis and Elliptic have all pointed to North Korea as being behind the Binance heist, with Chainalysis labeling the incident as “the largest in the history of crypto, and one of the single-largest financial crimes of all time.” The funds drained in the attack were a mix of the largest cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether, and the dollar-backed stablecoins USDT and USDC. Bitcoin fell on news of the Binance attack, dropping below $77,000 for the first time in more than a month. The largest currency traded near the lows of the day for much of Friday.   For the crypto faithful who’d been basking in a two-month-long price rebound, the Binance incident has cast a shadow over the recovery. Binance dwarfs its industry rivals. It holds roughly $135.2 billion in assets, compared with $28.6 billion at the second-largest exchange OKX, according to DefiLlama data.   Binance said the incident may involve a compromised software engineer’s laptop, as well as “additional points of breach.” It found no evidence of leaked private keys, it said. “This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it,” Binance said in a post on X. An emergency insurance and reserve fund from Binance called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) was established in 2018 to serve as a backstop for customers in “extreme situations,” according to the exchange. The SAFU is generally maintained at around $1 billion, but has fluctuated in the past in tandem with market movements, Binance said in 2024. The two biggest stablecoin issuers said they took steps to freeze affected currency. Paolo Ardoino, the chief executive officer of Tether, said in an X post that it froze more than $1.5 billion of the stablecoin USDT “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Jeremy Allaire, who runs Circle Internet Group Inc., said $800 million of its USDC token had been frozen amid “reports of a potential exploit involving Binance.”

item.title: US probing possible North Korean link to $6.3 bn Binance hack: Trump
item.description: The US president said Washington was investigating whether North Korean hackers were behind the record cryptocurrency theft, as Binance said about $3 billion of the stolen assets had been frozen ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Skylar Woodhouse President Donald Trump said the US was looking into whether North Korean hackers were behind a $6.3 billion heist targeting Binance that has rattled the cryptocurrency world. “We don’t know. We’re looking at that,” Trump told reporters Friday in the Oval Office when asked if the hack should be attributed to actors from North Korea. Hackers from that country have been known to prey on the digital asset industry and accused by the FBI and cybersecurity experts of involvement in some of the biggest crypto thefts in recent years. Binance, the world’s largest crypto trading platform, suspended withdrawals and pledged to cover all losses after the hack, the biggest heist the digital-asset industry has ever faced. Binance posted on X that about $3 billion of the assets had been frozen on blockchain networks. In another post, co-founder Yi He said withdrawals were expected to resume by Sunday. “They’re saying they’re guaranteeing it or something,” Trump said. “It was a hack. That’s the problem. You know the old-fashioned way when you used to sign a check, take it out. These are different people. Never see the money anymore. So I’ve always felt it was a little bit dangerous.” “They say they have it pretty much under control,” he added, referring to Binance. Binance has had ties to businesses connected to the president and his family. The firm helped develop a stablecoin for a company that Trump and his sons co-founded. Changpeng Zhao, Binance’s co-founder and former CEO, was pardoned by Trump in 2025 after he pleaded guilty to failing to enforce robust anti-money-laundering measures. The hacking incident came amid growing concern about the risks posed by hackers in the artificial intelligence age. It also marked a setback for an industry that is keen to expand its presence in traditional finance and which has benefitted from Trump’s push to ease regulatory burdens. Western governments have accused North Korea of fostering hacking groups and using them to bring in funds to pay for weapons programs. Trump in recent weeks has floated new US outreach to North Korea, suggesting that a potential meeting with its leader, Kim Jong Un, could happen this year. Earlier this month, however, Trump downplayed those expectations, saying he was “not sure that anybody’s asking for a meeting.”

item.content:encoded:
Home / India News / Isro's GSLV successfully places NVS-03 satellite into 'designated' orbit

Isro's GSLV successfully places NVS-03 satellite into 'designated' orbit The GSLV mission placed the second-generation navigation satellite into its designated orbit, restoring NavIC to 4 operational satellites and strengthening India's indigenous navigation

On NVS-03, the Isro chief said that all the vehicle systems performed as predicted, and as expected (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India Sriharikota (Andhra Pradesh) 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 31 2026 | 8:33 AM IST

Listen to This Article

India's independent regional navigation satellite system NavIC was restored to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites on Friday as Isro successfully launched its navigation satellite NVS-03, which was placed into the designated injection orbit by a GSLV rocket. The second-generation navigation satellite NVS-03 with indigenous and procured atomic clocks has a wide array of applications including civilian use like real time tracking of trains, vehicles, and shipping vessels. Further, the NavIC constellation is an important component of the 'one nation, one time' project, Isro chief V Narayanan said after the successful mission launch. The NVS-03 satellite is all set to complement three other navigational satellites in operation including the NVS-01 and it will strengthen infrastructure for a robust IST with the government recently notifying the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026. The nation's own satellite navigation system 'NaVIC,' is the Indian version of GPS, albeit confined to the country and 1,500 km beyond.

On Friday, the 50-metre-tall GSLV rocket carrying NVS-03 lifted off at the scheduled time of 11.51 pm from the second launch pad at Satish Dhawan Space Centre, following a 24-hour countdown. Also Read

After a flight of about 18 minutes, which saw the successful performance of all three stages including the complex cryogenic upper stage, the primary payload got separated from the launch vehicle and was injected into a Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO). In his address following the success of the crucial mission, Narayanan said already three satellites, including NVS-01 are successfully working and now, NVS-03 has restored Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) services.

"NavIC ((Navigation with Indian Constellation) is a strategic national asset which provides independent access to Position, Navigation, Timing services, and it is also used for civilian applications like real time tracking of trains, vehicles, shipping vessels," he said. Further, he asserted that the NavIC constellation is an important component of the 'one nation, one time' project. Speaking on the constellation, he said that one of the indigenous atomic clocks had already been placed in the orbit. He announced that the EOS-05 geo imaging satellite, launched in September, was working perfectly and that the space agency is getting "outstanding" data from it. On NVS-03, the Isro chief said that all the vehicle systems performed as predicted, and as expected. The GSLV rocket, in its 20th flight, successfully, and precisely injected NVS-03 satellite into the designated orbit.

"The NVS-03 satellite mission has been accomplished with the least turnaround time of 56 days between successive GSLV missions," he said. He congratulated the entire Isro team, industrial partners, and academia for the outstanding accomplishment, and for the success of the mission. Also, he said that almost 80 per cent of the budget has been "pumped into the Indian industries."   The targeted orbit of NVS-03 has a planned perigee (closest point to Earth) of 170 km and an apogee (farthest point) of 37,023 km. The 2,232 kg NVS-03 satellite will subsequently use its onboard propulsion to reach its final Geosynchronous slot at 32.5 degrees East. To ensure propulsion system reliability, Isro flew the satellite with its pyrotechnic valves already open, an unprecedented safety measure adopted for this mission.

The satellite, which features an indigenous Rubidium atomic clock, is a crucial addition to the NavIC system and will transmit signals in the L1, L5, and S bands to strengthen India's regional positioning services. Meanwhile, Union MoS (Independent Charge) Science & Technology, Jitendra Singh congratulated Team Isro for the successful launch of GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission. "This remarkable achievement reflects India's growing prowess in Space technology and our unwavering commitment to strengthening sovereign indigenous navigation capabilities. With revolutionary Space reforms announced by PM Shri @narendramodi ji in recent years, India's success stories in Space vindicate the dream of founding fathers Vikram Sarabhai and Satish Dhawan. Today is the celebration of another proud moment for India," he said in a social media post.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)
